body:
Claiming a narrow fix inside app/renderer, which Rosalind (S008) has now released. Supervisor's report,
verbatim: "After entering the model settings i can't close the settings window."

Reproduced from the source, and it is two independent closed doors on the same sheet.

1. The close button scrolls out of reach. `.drawer` is `position: fixed` with
   `max-height: calc(100vh - var(--rail) - var(--transport, 76px) - 16px)` and `overflow: auto`, but
   `.drawer-bar` — the flex row holding the ✕ at ConfigDrawer.tsx:88 — is an ordinary child with no
   `position: sticky`. So the moment the content is taller than the sheet, the bar scrolls up and away with
   it. "After entering the model settings" is exactly what makes it tall: typing a base_url starts the
   debounced `onFetchModels()` at 700ms, the endpoint's model list lands, and the sheet grows past its cap.
   The control that dismisses the sheet is then outside the visible area, with nothing on screen saying so.

2. Escape is inert where the focus actually is. ConfigDrawer.tsx:76 ignores Escape whenever focus is in an
   INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT. The comment says "mid-word", which suggests IME composition was the worry; the code
   ignores Escape in any text field, and after typing a base_url or a model name that is where the focus is.
   So the keyboard exit is off too, in the exact state the supervisor was in when they typed.

Both roads out fail at once, which is why it reads as "stuck" rather than "awkward".

Scope: `app/renderer/styles.css` (`.drawer-bar` only) and `app/renderer/shell/ConfigDrawer.tsx` (the Escape
guard only, and only the INPUT/TEXTAREA part of it). No visual language changes — Rosalind's grammar (ice =
live, amber = belief, serif/mono split) is untouched, and nothing about the sheet's composition moves. This is
a control-availability fix, not a design opinion.

Verification, because this is a CSS/layout defect and the repo's own lesson is that the suite cannot see one
(Mara's session: 168 renderer assertions passed while the transport bar was dead, because none of them render
CSS): the fix gets driven in a real Electron window on its own debug port and `--user-data-dir`, the way
Rosalind did their pass, with the sheet forced into the tall state that triggers the bug. The pre-commit gate
runs too, but it is not the evidence.

Also in scope, and cheap: a renderer assertion for the Escape behaviour, which is pure logic and can be
tested without a window — the one half of this that a test can honestly hold.

Not touching: the rest of app/renderer, though Rosalind has released it; `panels/`, `core/` and the run view
are theirs and stay as they left them. Not attempting the second half of the supervisor's report (being asked
for the API key again on every launch) here — the key is session-only by deliberate design, so changing that
is a security decision for the supervisor, not a bug fix I should take unilaterally.
